targetAudience.primary: Engineers building concurrent file-backed runtimes, migrations and recovery workers
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands discovery, locks, mutable paths and retryable lifecycle states.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A worker can act on a path or emptiness observation that became stale before it acquired authority to mutate the resource.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change hardens startup rollout migration with post-lock rereads, path rediscovery, retryable busy state and separate terminal failure.

externalHook.description: Discovery locates a mutable resource; only post-authority revalidation can justify mutation.

coreProposition: For mutable runtime resources, discovery is provisional evidence rather than execution authority: after writer ownership is acquired and before mutation, revalidate logical identity, current location and decision-relevant state, while keeping busy contention distinct from terminal failure.

originalValue.description: Separates stable logical identity from mutable locator and turns post-claim reread into a correctness obligation rather than a retry optimization.

readerTakeaway: Treat pre-lock observations as hints, re-resolve the resource after authority acquisition, and model busy, failed and completed outcomes as different lifecycle facts.

supported: Rollout paths can be rediscovered after NotFound or archive/compression movement.
Apparently empty rollouts are reread while holding the writer lock.
Writer contention remains busy and retryable while terminal failure is recorded separately.
uncertain: Which stable identity should survive every path transition
When repeated busy outcomes should escalate

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general mutable-resource concurrency pattern without a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged mechanisms and concurrency regressions support a transferable post-authority revalidation discipline with explicit scope.
